 *  Named `disabled` (not e.g. `isUnavailable`) to match the resolution-prop convention already
 *  used by every other function-form baseStyle in this codebase (zimmTextInput.css.ts's own
 *  `disabled` key) — `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s PROP_COMBINATIONS harness only
 *  exercises the fixed key set `{inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled}`, so a
 *  differently-named boolean here would never have its `true` branch walked by that guard. */
export type ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps = {
  disabled?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe — cart-line quantity stepper (SFCC-271). Two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls sit
 * either side of a numeric value display; all hover/press/focus/disabled states for the buttons
 * themselves live entirely in zimmButton.css.ts (untouched by this file — see index.tsx, which
 * composes ZimmButton rather than restyling it).
 *
 * `root` — the flex row. Gap is 8px (`var(--zimm-scale-xs)` — foundation/spacing.ts's `xs` is
 * `0.5rem`/8px exactly, so this needs no new token). Deliberate, disclosed departure from
 * Figma's own raw annotation, which shows a 12px gap around a bare 12px glyph with no drawn
 * touch target at all. ZimmButton's `icon` size variant already resolves both buttons to a 24px
 * touch target (zimmButton.css.ts `sizes.icon` — `minW`/`minH`: `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, cited
 * there against WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8, and matching the Figma node's own literal name
 * `touchTarget` at value 24) — i.e. 6px of invisible padding is already added on every side of
 * each 12px glyph before this gap is even applied. An 8px authored gap between the two 24px
 * button boxes therefore reproduces the ~12px glyph-to-glyph spacing Figma's raw annotation
 * intended (6px inset + 8px gap + 6px inset from centre-of-glyph to centre-of-glyph ≈ the
 * annotated 12px), without shrinking either button below its accessible 24px target — the
 * alternative (an 8px gap measured glyph-edge to glyph-edge with no inset accounted for) would
 * under-space them relative to Figma; this recipe's 8px is the touch-target-aware equivalent,
 * not a straight copy of the raw annotation.
 *
 * `value` — the numeric display. No Figma node or type-style was supplied for this specific text
 * in this build step; `body2Strong` (14px / 500 weight / 18px line-height, typography.ts) is the
 * nearest existing textStyle — PROVISIONAL pending UI-designer confirmation, same disclosure
 * pattern as zimmSizeSelector.css.ts's own oneSize label. Dims to OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED when
 * `disabled` (the whole control is OOS/unavailable, not just one bound) — sourced from
 * zimmCartItemShared.ts rather than restated here or imported from zimmButton.css.ts, so the
 * value display and the two buttons beside it (which get their own dimming entirely from
 * zimmButton.css.ts's `icon` variant, once the caller passes `ariaDisabled` through — nothing
 * about that is duplicated here) can never visually drift apart, without this recipe reaching
 * into an unrelated atom's styling module for the number. Applying the SAME opacity to `root`
 * as well would double it up on the buttons (0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16, not 0.4) — deliberately scoped to
 * `value` only for that reason.
 */
export const ZimmQuantityStepper = {
  parts: ['root', 'value'],
  baseStyle: ({ disabled }: ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    root: {
      display: 'inline-flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
    },
    value: {
      display: 'inline-flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      justifyContent: 'center',
      textStyle: 'body2Strong',
      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
      opacity: disabled ? OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED : 1,
    },
  }),
};

1	// Co-located recipe for ZimmBadge — Figma node 40001471:20752 (Zimmermann_Design_System_2026,
2	// State=Primary / State=Hover). Registered in theme/components/index.ts. Per
3	// .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's co-location pattern, governance follows this file's own
4	// CODEOWNERS entry (owning squad), not theme/components/'s Tier 2 UI-designer gate.
5	// Figma 40001471:20751 (Primary): white box, 1px border, 4px padding, centred label. Shared by
6	// both the interactive `link` part and the non-interactive `staticBox` part below — factored out
7	// so a hover affordance can't leak onto the static variant just because the two share a look.
8	const badgeBox = {
9	  display: 'flex',
10	  alignItems: 'center',
11	  justifyContent: 'center',
12	  alignContent: 'stretch',
13	  padding: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)', // 4px
14	  border: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
15	  backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-07)',
16	  position: 'relative',
17	  textDecoration: 'none',
18	  // ZimmProductBadges' row is a flex container with flexWrap:nowrap (Figma-confirmed) — without
19	  // this, a badge with a long label gets its BOX shrunk to fit the row while the label inside
20	  // (already flexShrink:0) refuses to shrink, so the text spills past the now-too-narrow
21	  // border. This is what stops that: the badge box itself never shrinks below its label's
22	  // natural width, matching the label's own flexShrink:0. See SFCC-132 long-label review.
23	  flexShrink: 0,
24	};
25	
26	export const ZimmBadge = {
27	  parts: ['link', 'staticBox', 'label'],
28	  baseStyle: {
29	    // Used only when ZimmBadge renders a real <a> (safe href present) — carries the hover
30	    // affordance, since this is the only variant that's actually clickable.
31	    link: {
32	      ...badgeBox,
33	      // Hover recolours both the border (here) and the nested label text (below) — written on
34	      // this part because the label's own box doesn't necessarily cover every padding pixel of
35	      // the link, so a hover rule scoped to the label alone could miss a pointer resting in the
36	      // padding. Figma names these aliases action/primary/bg/hover and
37	      // action/secondary/text/disabled — both resolve to the same #969696 (zimm grey/300) and
38	      // are applied here to border/text, not the "bg"/"disabled" purpose their names suggest.
39	      // That's Figma's own aliasing choice, confirmed against the file's variable defs — not a
40	      // mistake in this recipe. See SFCC-132.
41	      _hover: {
42	        borderColor: 'var(--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover)',
43	        '.zimm-badge-label': {
44	          color: 'var(--zimm-color-action-secondary-text-disabled)',
45	        },
46	      },
47	    },
48	    // Used when ZimmBadge renders the non-interactive <span> fallback (no/unsafe href) —
49	    // identical box, deliberately WITHOUT _hover: a badge that isn't clickable shouldn't react
50	    // to a pointer resting on it as though it were (CodeRabbit finding, SFCC-132 review).
51	    staticBox: {
52	      ...badgeBox,
53	    },
54	    // Composite "Default/Input-label" typography (10px size / 500 weight / 18px line-height /
55	    // 0 letter-spacing) has no registered textStyle in typography.ts — the closest entries
56	    // (`footer`, `caption`) each diverge on at least one axis. Built from the same --zimm-font-*
57	    // primitives a matching textStyle would use, per overrideStyling.md hierarchy point 2's
58	    // individual-piece fallback — every value here already exists in zimmTokens.ts, nothing new
59	    // added to foundation/. If a second component ever needs this exact combination, promote it
60	    // to a named textStyles.inputLabel entry in typography.ts instead of copying this block.
61	    label: {
62	      fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-heading)', // medium (500) face
63	      fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-4xs)', // 10px
64	      fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)', // 500
65	      lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)', // 18px
66	      letterSpacing: 'var(--zimm-font-letterspacing-sm)', // 0
67	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
68	      // Not a bindable Figma variable — inferred from the rendered mock showing "LABEL" in caps.
69	      textTransform: 'uppercase',
70	      flexShrink: 0,
71	      wordBreak: 'break-word',
72	      // CSS Text Box Trim — trims the line-height dead space above cap-height/below the
73	      // alphabetic baseline so the label's box matches Figma's measured 15px badge height
74	      // despite an 18px line-height. Provisional: new to this codebase, no other component
75	      // relies on it yet — confirm browser support before treating it as a safe default
76	      // elsewhere. See SFCC-132 design-token audit.
77	      textBoxTrim: 'trim-both',
78	      textBoxEdge: 'cap alphabetic',
79	      // Figma's export sets a fixed w-[25px] on this text node — that's just the auto-measured
80	      // width of the literal placeholder "LABEL" (5 characters), not a fixed-width design
81	      // intent. Confirmed with the UI designer (SFCC-132): badge width is auto-length, sized
82	      // to whatever label it holds — no width set here is deliberate, not an omission.
83	    },
84	  },
85	};

5	 * string: label at x=0 (57px wide) and value at x=61 (157px wide) inside the 218px info

7	 * sample copy, not a spec, and fixing them would break the moment the label is translated
8	 * (11 locales). The gap between them is the part that carries meaning: 61 - 57 = 4px, which
9	 * is exactly `spacing['2xs']`.
10	 *
11	 * Open with the designer (see the PR body): the DS models this as two nodes while both
12	 * composed page designs show a single concatenated string, "Style Code: 7300JS261". A flex
13	 * row of two nodes renders identically to the concatenation, so this satisfies both until the
14	 * question is settled.
15	 *
16	 * Type sits on `root` rather than on the element. `@chakra-ui/system`'s `toCSSObject` assigns
17	 * `styleProps` *after* `__css` (`assignAfter({}, __css, finalBaseStyle,
18	 * filterUndefined(styleProps), sx)`, dist/index.js lines 204-213), and `assignAfter` re-inserts a
19	 * duplicate key — so a `textStyle=` on the JSX would displace this one. `root` is the right part:
20	 * `label` and `value` inherit the type from it, so it is declared once, not on each of the two.
21	 */
22	export const ZimmProductStyleCode = {
23	  parts: ['root', 'label', 'value'],
24	
25	  baseStyle: (): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
26	    root: {
27	      display: 'flex',
28	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xs)',
29	      textStyle: 'caption',
30	      // Figma Zimmermann_Designs 3093:67151 specifies `alias/color/text/secondary` (#666666) for
31	      // this line, not the default text colour — the style code is deliberately quieter than the
32	      // copy above it. Our `--zimm-color-text-secondary` resolves to grey[600] = #666666, an exact
33	      // match. The model line above it does use the default colour; the two differ by design.
34	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)',
35	    },
36	    label: {
37	      margin: 0,
38	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
39	    },
40	    value: {
41	      margin: 0,
42	    },
43	  }),

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { useIntl } from 'react-intl';
4	
5	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_STYLE_CODE_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductStyleCode';
6	
7	/*
8	 * The label is UI copy, so it is a translatable message rather than a literal. `defaultMessage`
9	 * carries the English inline, which is what makes this work with no `translations/` entry: that
10	 * directory is Tier 2 (owner Integration/SI Partner) and is populated by the extraction step, so
11	 * a component cannot add to it. Until extraction runs, every locale renders `defaultMessage`;
12	 * once it does, the eleven locales pick up their own string with no change here.
13	 *
14	 * The id follows the base template's namespace for PDP labels — `product_view.label.quantity`
15	 * and `product_view.label.variant_type` are its siblings — so a translator finds it with the
16	 * rest of the PDP copy.
17	 */
18	const LABEL_MESSAGE = {
19	  id: 'product_view.label.style_code',
20	  defaultMessage: 'Style Code:',
21	};
22	
23	type ZimmProductStyleCodeProps = {
24	  /**
25	   * The master product's style number. This is the style code shown to shoppers, which is not
26	   * the same value as the variant `product.id`.
27	   */
28	  value?: string;
29	};
30	
31	/**
32	 * Atom — the "Style Code: 7300JS261" line. Renders nothing when no style code is available.
33	 *
34	 * The label comes from `react-intl`, not from CMS microcopy and not from a literal. A `uiCopy`
35	 * lookup is the wrong tool here — `useContentful.ts` requests entries with no `locale`
36	 * parameter, so it would serve the space default to all eight storefronts regardless of site —
37	 * but a bare literal is not the remedy for that, it just ships English to all eleven locales
38	 * instead. `formatMessage` is the base template's own mechanism and is per-locale by
39	 * construction.
40	 *
41	 * components.md exempts `useIntl` from the container/presentational rule: it reads a Provider
42	 * mounted above the route tree, so calling it from a leaf creates none of the per-page fetch
43	 * problems that rule exists to prevent. It does *throw* without an `IntlProvider` — the app
44	 * mounts one in the base `_app`, `.storybook/preview.tsx` mounts one for stories, and
45	 * `index.test.tsx` wraps its renders for the same reason.
46	 */
47	export const ZimmProductStyleCode = ({ value }: ZimmProductStyleCodeProps) => {
48	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_STYLE_CODE_RECIPE, {});
49	  // `intl.formatMessage`, not a destructured `{ formatMessage }`: destructuring a method off
50	  // `useIntl()` trips `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`, which `staticProductHeader.tsx` has to
51	  // suppress inline. `product-view/index.tsx` uses this form throughout and needs no suppression.
52	  const intl = useIntl();
53	  // Both hooks sit above the guard: an early return before either makes that call conditional,
54	  // which `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` reports as an error. Same ordering as the sibling atoms.
55	  if (!value) return null;
56	
57	  return (
58	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-style-code">
59	      <chakra.span __css={styles.label}>{intl.formatMessage(LABEL_MESSAGE)}</chakra.span>
60	      {/*
61	        A real space so `textContent` — what a screen reader reads out and what a shopper
62	        copies — is "Style Code: 8637DS241", matching both composed page designs. It adds no
63	        visual width: a whitespace-only anonymous flex item is not rendered (CSS Flexbox §4),
64	        so the 4px `gap` in the recipe remains the only spacing.
65	      */}{' '}
66	      <chakra.span __css={styles.value}>{value}</chakra.span>
67	    </chakra.div>
68	  );
69	};

99	export const GROW_UNDERLINE_SX: SystemStyleObject = {

101	    position: 'relative',
102	    borderBottom: 'none',
103	  },
104	  '& > span::after': {
105	    content: '""',
106	    position: 'absolute',
107	    left: 0,
108	    right: 0,

| Recommended-for-you chevrons | **24x24** | 16 |
| drawer/header close | **44h x 24w** | 16 |
| **Cart item stepper +/-** | **none** | **12** |

"44" has provenance (close-button height) but **nothing in the design is 44x44**, which is what
SFCC-795's AC asks for. And the stepper has no touch target at all — 12px, half the 24px the rest
of the system uses. Per the house pattern (`zimmButton.css.ts`): annotate inline citing the
criterion and the source, add to the UI designer's open list, ship. Also **ask the designer whether
the stepper icons should get the same 24px touchTarget** — it reads as an oversight, not intent.

## 11.9 Design-side issues to raise

- stepper icons 12px with no touch target, against a 24px system convention
- `25px` used twice as an untokenised raw value (Item Actions gap; empty-bag paragraph spacing)
- two token namespaces coexist: `brand/font/*` + `alias/*` vs `default/*` + `line-height/*`
- two tokens resolve to the same #969696 (`text/subtlest` vs `text/muted`)
- stacked success drops the product name; single success keeps it
- SFCC-272 copy conflicts: design "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist" vs AC "[Product Name]
  has been moved to your wishlist"; design already-in-wishlist is a **warning** ("An item in your
  bag already exists in Wishlist") vs AC's **error** banner with different wording.
  Cards say "figma leading" => design wins, but record the divergence on 272.
- ~~empty-bag Client Services details are hardcoded AU~~ — **NOT an issue for this build**
  (Marcel, 2026-09-16): we ship a placeholder empty state only; the real one is SFCC-277's.
  **But the question carries to SFCC-277** — the design hardcodes `+61 1800 738 895`,
  "Monday – Saturday: 9:00AM – 5:30PM" and `clientservices@zimmermann.com` across 8 storefronts /
  6 regions. Which of those vary per region, and are hours shown in local or AU time?
  Flag on 277 at grooming so it isn't rediscovered mid-build.

## 11.10 Design open items — RESOLVED (2026-09-16)

**(4) `25px` raw value — DECIDED (Marcel): implement 24px** (`--zimm-scale-xl`… actually
`space/600`), with a short comment noting the design specified 25 and it was snapped to the nearest
tokenised value. Applies to the Item Actions gap and the empty-bag paragraph spacing.

**(5) Two token namespaces — RESOLVED from the codebase.** Our `--zimm-font-*` vars mirror
`brand/font/*`'s shape (family / size / lineheight / letterspacing), not `default/*` +
`line-height/*`. So `brand/font/*` is the current generation; the `default/*` usages (empty-bag
body, promo accordion) are the older one.
**More useful: our 22 registered textStyles map near 1:1 to the Figma named styles** — map style→
textStyle, not var-by-var:
`Default/body2`→`body2` · `body2-strong`→`body2Strong` · `Caption`→`caption` ·
`Link-sm`→`linkSm` · `Product-name`/`Product Names`→`productNames` · `Price`→`price` ·
`Button-lg`→`button` · `Body 1`→`body1` · `Body 2 Medium`→`body2Strong`
**Two gaps:** no `captionStrong` for Figma's `Default/Caption-strong` (the cart item's colour+size
line, medium/500) — we only have `caption`. And `mobileBody1`/`mobileBody2`/`mobileBody1Strong`
exist, so there are mobile-specific styles to consider for the reflow.

**(6) Two tokens for #969696 — RESOLVED from the codebase.** We have
`text.muted = grey[300] = #969696` and **no `subtlest`**. Both Figma names collapse onto
**`--zimm-color-text-muted`**. No ambiguity in our system.
**Bonus — every colour in the cart design already exists in our foundation. No new tokens needed:**
| Figma | Ours |
|---|---|
| `text/default` #191919 | `grey[900]` → `--zimm-color-text-default` |
| `text/subtle` #666 | `grey[600]` → `text.secondary` |
| `text/subtlest` + `text/muted` #969696 | `grey[300]` → `text.muted` |
| `text/error` #9c0000 | `red[500]` → **`status.error`** |
| `text/success` #2d5a3d | `green[500]` → **`status.success`** |
| `bg/surface/default` #f6f4f1 | `ivory[200]` |
| `border/default` #e6e6e6 | `grey[100]` → `border.default` |

**(7) Warning typography — DRIFT, conclusively.** Checked desktop + mobile. The WARNINGS SHOWN
state is off-pattern in **four** ways at both breakpoints:
- `Default/Body 2 Medium` (Medium/500, ls −0.14px) vs every other message's `Default/body2`
  (regular/400, ls 0)
- **`px-[128px]` hardcoded** instead of `var(--alias/space/3200)` — and it is on a **mobile** frame
  where the gutter should be 32px
- **`text-[#969696]` hardcoded hex** instead of the token var
- `Page-level-message` `w-full` instead of the established `w-[476px]`
Its mobile header is also 68px where the default mobile frame's is 108px.
=> built separately, off-pattern. **Implement WARNINGS SHOWN using the established message pattern**
   (body2, `--zimm-color-text-muted`, tokenised gutter), not its own styling.

**(8) Stacked success drops the product name — INTENTIONAL by prevalence.** Generic
("Item added to Wishlist") at **both** desktop and mobile in the stacked state; product-named
("Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist") in the single state. Consistent in both states, so per
the one-off-vs-prevalent test it is deliberate compaction.
**But worth confirming rather than silently following:** it drops the single most useful piece of
information exactly when there is more on screen, and it conflicts with SFCC-272's AC, which
specifies `[Product Name]` in all cases.

**(9) Odd computed numbers — ROOT FOUND. Two separate causes.**
- **The decimal paddings are post-scale rendered values of real tokens.** Proof: `alias/space/1200`
  reports fallback **48px** on the empty-bag cart-item-group gap and **12.655px** on the cart item
  image; `alias/space/1000` reports **40px** on the header/recommendations and **8.944px** on the
  mobile cart item image. Same token, different fallback => the decimal is what Figma rendered after
  scaling, not the token value. **Use the token (48 / 40), never the decimal.**
- **Tablet 659.2 is a computed fill width, not a spec.** `659.2 = 595.2 content + 2 × 32 gutter`;

21	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2).
22	 *
23	 * Parts:
24	 *   - `image` — item-image.tsx's outer Box: responsive width, ivory-200 background. Applied
25	 *     via `__css`, not `sx` — this one MUST stay overridable: order-summary/index.jsx (base
26	 *     SFCC, not yet overridden in this repo) calls
27	 *     `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` and depends on its own caller-supplied
28	 *     `width` winning over whatever default this component ships. `__css` is the lowest-
29	 *     priority slot in `@chakra-ui/system`'s `toCSSObject` merge (`chunk-E32MZNBA.mjs`:
30	 *     `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)`), and `Box` carries no competing
31	 *     baseStyle of its own (`@chakra-ui/layout`'s `chunk-6CSUKJP7.mjs`: `var Box =
32	 *     chakra("div")`, no options) — confirmed by reading both files, not assumed — so a
33	 *     literal caller prop always wins over this part's `__css` default.
34	 *   - `img` — the inner <Image>: responsive objectFit (contain mobile / cover desktop) plus
35	 *     mix-blend-multiply, so the photo blends against the `image` part's ivory backdrop.
36	 *     `__css` is safe here too — Chakra's own `Image` (`@chakra-ui/image`'s
37	 *     `chunk-SMHKDLMK.mjs`) never sets a literal `__css` key of its own, unlike `Text` below.
38	 *   - `colourSize` — item-attributes.tsx's combined "colour, size" string.
39	 *   - `price` — item-price.tsx's price Stack (`textStyle: 'price'` only; the actual price
40	 *     digits render via the base, un-overridden `display-price`/`current-price` components,
41	 *     which set no competing font-size of their own — confirmed by reading both files — so
42	 *     the textStyle cascades down via ordinary CSS inheritance without touching either file).
43	 *
44	 * `colourSize` and `price` are applied via `sx`, not `__css`: Chakra's own `Text`
45	 * (`@chakra-ui/layout`'s `chunk-P74GIWPW.mjs`) places its OWN `__css={styles}` (from
46	 * `useStyleConfig('Text', props)`) as a literal key AFTER `...rest` in its own render call —
47	 * a caller-supplied `__css` prop would be silently discarded entirely there (a later
48	 * same-named key in one object literal replaces the earlier one; it does not merge). `sx` is
49	 * destructured separately by `toCSSObject` and isn't subject to that collision, so it's the
50	 * reliable way to style a plain `<Text>`/`<Stack>` from outside. Verified by reading the
51	 * compiled source directly. `price`'s own Stack has no such hazard (`@chakra-ui/layout`'s
52	 * `chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs` Stack sets no literal `__css` key at all), so either mechanism would
53	 * have worked there — `sx` is used anyway, for one consistent rule across this file's parts
54	 * rather than a different mechanism per element.

61	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-02)',

77	      // node, not the regular-weight "Default/Caption" node — .claude/session-notes.md says so

79	      // ONE combined string ... `Default/Caption-strong` 12px / lh18") and §11.10(5) ("no

1	/**
2	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework, extended post-rework (found live in Storybook by Marcel, not by this
3	 * suite). Proves three stacked bugs are actually fixed TOGETHER, not just that the symbols were
4	 * added:
5	 *   1. `useVariationAttributes` -> `isVariantValueOrderable` (base SFCC hook, unconditional
6	 *      `product.variants.filter(...)`) needs `variants` to be an array on the mock product.
7	 *   2. `useDerivedProduct` unconditionally calls `useSelectedStore()`, which throws without a
8	 *      real `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor.
9	 *   3. `item-attributes.tsx`'s `useCurrentBasket()` call has its own separate transitive chain
10	 *      (`useSFPayments` -> `useAppOrigin` -> `useOrigin`) that calls the SDK's
11	 *      `useServerContext()` and destructures `res` from it unconditionally, before `useOrigin`'s
12	 *      own `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch (which never touches `res`) is reached. This
13	 *      file previously mocked `useCurrentBasket` away entirely, which hid this bug completely —
14	 *      unmocked now so this suite actually exercises the real chain. `ServerContext.Provider`
15	 *      with `value={{}}` matches exactly what the real app's own browser bootstrap supplies
16	 *      client-side (`ssr/browser/main.js`'s `OuterApp`) — confirmed by reading that file.
17	 *
18	 * Deliberately does NOT use index.test.tsx's harness — that file mocks the whole
19	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks` barrel's `useDerivedProduct`, which would hide both
20	 * bugs this file exists to catch. This renders through the real, unmocked `useDerivedProduct` ->
21	 * `useVariationAttributes` -> `isVariantValueOrderable` / `useSelectedStore` chain, with a real
22	 * `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor.
23	 *
24	 * `useMultiSite` and `useCurrency` are still mocked, for a reason that has nothing to do with
25	 * this build's own logic: `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts` (the barrel both
26	 * `MultiSiteProvider`/`CurrencyProvider` and `use-multi-site.js`/`use-currency.js` resolve
27	 * through) is a `.js` file containing inline JSX, which Vite's transform cannot parse as a
28	 * plain `.js` file — confirmed empirically (this file's first draft imported `MultiSiteProvider`
29	 * from that barrel directly and vitest failed at import-analysis on
30	 * `app/contexts/index.js:49`, not at any assertion). This is the same parse failure
31	 * item-variant/index.test.tsx's own docblock already documents and works around by mocking
32	 * `use-multi-site` instead of using a real `MultiSiteProvider`; extended here to `useCurrency`
33	 * for the same reason. `StoreLocatorProvider` itself is real: `use-selected-store.js` and
34	 * `store-locator-provider.jsx` both import `StoreLocatorContext` via that file's own direct path
35	 * (`.../app/contexts/store-locator-provider`), never through the barrel, so it never hits this
36	 * parse wall — confirmed by reading both files' imports, not assumed.
37	 *
38	 * Two more pragmatic mocks, both explained inline at their own `vi.mock`/`beforeEach`: `useStores`
39	 * (an unrelated dual-module-instance QueryClient issue, not this build's own code) and a
40	 * `window.matchMedia` polyfill (jsdom has none; item-price.tsx's `useBreakpointValue` needs it —
41	 * the same pre-existing gap and fix product-item/index.test.tsx's own `beforeEach` already uses).
42	 * Neither affects what this file actually proves: that a real `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor and
43	 * an array-valued `variants` together stop the render from throwing.
44	 */
45	import React from 'react';
46	import { describe, test, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';

/**
 * Co-located recipe for the cart line-item shell (overrides/app/components/product-item).
 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2) — restyles the copy-first port to the Figma-sourced cart-item spec.
 *
 * Parts:
 *   - `row` — the image + item-details row. Figma: gap 28px desktop / 24px mobile, align
 *     centre desktop / start mobile.
 *   - `details` — the column beside the image (name/attrs/price/stepper/actions). Figma:
 *     gap 12px desktop / 24px mobile.
 *   - `info` — the name + colour/size (+ mobile price) block, paired with the desktop-only
 *     delivery-actions slot. Figma: column layout desktop / row + justify-space-between
 *     mobile. The mobile values match this block's pre-existing unconditional layout exactly
 *     (row, space-between, align flex-end) so nothing changes below `md` — only the desktop
 *     column switch is new.
 *
 * Applied via `sx`, not `__css`, though the two parts of this file's `Flex`/`Stack` pair get
 * there for different reasons — corrected here (round 2 rework) after reading both chunks
 * directly rather than assuming they behave alike:
 *   - `Stack` (`chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs`) passes its own computed `alignItems`/`justifyContent`/
 *     `flexDirection`/`gap` as SEPARATE literal props ahead of `{...rest}` in its own render
 *     (`jsx(chakra.div, {..., alignItems: align, ..., gap: spacing, ...rest})`). Those land in
 *     `@chakra-ui/system`'s `toCSSObject` (`chunk-E32MZNBA.mjs`) `styleProps` tier —
 *     `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)` — which sits ABOVE `__css`, so a
 *     `__css`-applied value from this recipe would be silently outranked by Stack's own `gap`
 *     whenever this component also sets one. `sx` (last, unconditionally winning) avoids that.
 *   - `Flex` (`chunk-MPFPK3CX.mjs`) does NOT do the same thing — it does not pass `align`/
 *     `justify`/`direction` as separate literal props at all. It bundles all of them into ONE
 *     `__css` object, placed BEFORE `{...rest}` (`jsx(chakra.div, {ref, __css: styles, ...rest})`).
 *     That is the same silent-full-object-discard mechanism `item-variant.css.ts`'s own docblock
 *     documents for `Text` — a later same-named key in one object literal replaces the earlier
 *     one, it does not merge — just with the winner reversed: a caller-supplied `__css` prop
 *     arriving via `rest` would silently discard Flex's OWN align/justify/direction/etc
 *     translation entirely, not the other way around. `sx` is a different prop name, so it never
 *     collides with either `__css` at this level — it flows through `rest` untouched and is
 *     merged in later, last, by the same `toCSSObject` call. Net effect for this file is
 *     unchanged either way: `sx` is safe and correct on both `Flex` and `Stack` here, regardless
 *     of which mechanism is in play.
 */
export const ZimmCartItem = {
  parts: ['row', 'details', 'info'],
  baseStyle: {
    row: {
      flexDirection: 'row',
      alignItems: 'flex-start',
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px mobile
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        alignItems: 'center',
        gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-700)', // 28px desktop
      },
    },
    details: {
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px mobile
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-s)', // 12px desktop
      },
    },
    info: {
      flexDirection: 'row',
      justifyContent: 'space-between',
      alignItems: 'flex-end',
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        flexDirection: 'column',
        alignItems: 'flex-start',
        justifyContent: 'flex-start',
      },
    },
  },
};

content.text:
All work is done and verified. Here's the report.

## What this step does, in one line

Cart line-items can now show a grey/red one-line note ("Quantity unavailable in this size", etc.) between the quantity stepper and the action buttons — but nothing turns it on yet. That's deliberate: turning it on is two other tickets (SFCC-282, SFCC-796), not this one.

## Files touched

**Created** (all three named in the plan, plus two test files the pass criteria require but the manifest didn't spell out — see note below):
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.stories.tsx`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/zimmInlineMessage.css.ts`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/zimmInlineMessage.css.test.ts` — not in the manifest, but pass criterion 2 explicitly requires "the recipe test"; matches the existing `zimmBadge.css.test.ts` co-located pattern.
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/product-item.css.test.ts` — same reasoning, for pass criterion 3 ("`product-item.css.ts`'s recipe test").

**Modified** (all named in the plan, plus the existing test file the DOM-order/no-regression criteria require):
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/product-item.css.ts`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx` — extended, not rewritten.

I did not touch `item-variant/*`, `zimmQuantityStepper/`, `zimmCartDrawer/`, `theme/foundation/`, or `product-item/index.stories.tsx` (no message-prop story was requested by the manifest or pass criteria, so I left it — cheap follow-up if wanted, not done here).

## Pass criteria, with evidence

**1. Stories: Error, Warning, plus one per exact string (≥5 total).** 5 stories in `index.stories.tsx`: `Default` (error/"This item is unavailable"), `ErrorVariant` (error/"Quantity unavailable in this size"), `Warning` (warning/"Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size"), `PartiallyOutOfStock` (error, 2nd string again), `MaxQuantityReached` (warning, 3rd string again). Named `ErrorVariant` not `Error` — exporting a const literally named `Error` shadows the JS global `Error` in that module, which I judged worth avoiding rather than matching the brief's word choice literally. Both variants and all 3 exact strings each appear in a real story, with the overlap the brief explicitly sanctioned.

**2. Colour tokens, asserted against the var string.** `zimmInlineMessage.css.test.ts`: `variants.error.color === 'var(--zimm-color-status-error)'` and `variants.warning.color === 'var(--zimm-color-text-muted)'`, both asserted `.not.toMatch(/#/)` too. Confirmed both are real registered aliases before writing anything (`colour.ts:81` `status.error = red[500] = #9c0000`, `colour.ts:68` `text.muted = grey[300] = #969696`) — matches the brief's own colours exactly, no invented token.

**3. `ZimmCartItem`'s `details` gap: 12px default, 16px on error.** `product-item.css.test.ts`, 4 tests, reading `ZimmCartItem.baseStyle({...})` directly: `hasError` omitted or `false` → desktop gap `var(--zimm-scale-s)` (12px); `hasError: true` → `var(--zimm-scale-m)` (16px, confirmed against `spacing.ts`: `m: '1rem' // 16px`); mobile gap (`var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, 24px) unchanged either way; `row`/`info` parts unaffected.

**4. DOM order, `compareDocumentPosition`.** `product-item/index.test.tsx`'s new test renders with `secondaryActions` and a `message`, then asserts `stepperNode.compareDocumentPosition(messageNode) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING` and `messageNode.compareDocumentPosition(actionsNode) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING` are both truthy — a real DOM-order check, not co-presence.

**5. `npm run audit:tokens` — no new unacknowledged raw values.** Ran it: 7 unacknowledged hits total, all pre-existing, all outside this step (`footer.css.ts`, `item-variant/item-image.tsx`, `item-variant/item-price.tsx`, `zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts`, `zimmDrawerShared.ts`). None of my files appear anywhere in the output — not flagged, not even in the acknowledged-exception list. Every value I wrote is a `var(--zimm-*)` token or a Chakra keyword (`'full'`).

**6. No low-stock variant anywhere.** `ZimmInlineMessageProps.variant` and `ProductItemProps.message.variant` are both exactly `'error' | 'warning'` (TS-checked, `tsc --noEmit` clean). Grepped both files: the only "low-stock" text is comments explaining its deliberate absence, and a test (`zimmInlineMessage.css.test.ts`) asserting `Object.keys(variants).sort()` is exactly `['error','warning']`.

**7. Existing callers unaffected.** New test `message omitted: nothing renders, and ZimmCartItem resolves hasError=false` — no message node in the DOM, and (via a spy on `useMultiStyleConfig` that still delegates to the real Chakra implementation) `ZimmCartItem` is called with `{hasError: false}`. Combined with criterion 3's recipe proof that `hasError:false` is the 12px value, this closes the loop without a fragile jsdom CSS-media-query assertion — see "one thing I deliberately didn't do" below for why I avoided that route. All pre-existing `product-item` tests (image/name/price/gift-card-slot/quantity-change) still pass unmodified.

`npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. `npm run test`: 91 files, 1295 tests, all green (includes `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s 6 hard-gate tests).

## The two design choices you asked me to name

**Prop shape:** `message?: {variant: 'error' | 'warning'; text: string}` on `ProductItemProps` — exactly the shape the brief suggested. `hasError` (the recipe-side flag) is derived inline as `message?.variant === 'error'`, not a second prop a caller sets independently — so the message and the gap can never disagree about whether an error is showing.

**Recipe-state prop name:** `hasError`, on `ZimmCartItem`'s now-function-form `baseStyle`. Chosen because `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s `PROP_COMBINATIONS` harness only ever exercises the fixed key set `{inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled}` — a differently-named boolean's `true` branch would never get walked by that guard, exactly the reasoning `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts` already documents for naming its own prop `disabled`. `ZimmCartItem.baseStyle` was a plain object before this commit; I converted it to a function, which is the one place the brief's wording was loosest ("read the current recipe's function-form baseStyle signature first" — it didn't have one yet, so I'm reporting that I built it, following the established shape, not that I found it pre-existing).

## Things I checked so I wouldn't have to guess

- The design record (`.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2) explicitly specifies this element as `Default/Caption regular 12px / lh18` with no icon — the earlier, vaguer summary line mentioning "grey info icon + message" turns out to describe the separate cart-level-messages component (§11.3, SFCC-404, a different ticket), not this one. No conflict, so nothing to escalate.
- The `caption`→regular-weight override and the earlier `caption`→medium-weight (no override) decision on the colour+size line are genuinely two different Figma nodes; I cited the real lines (`item-variant/item-variant.css.ts:73-84`) rather than asserting it from memory.
